claim: "Pizzagate" — the conspiracy theory that emerged in October 2016 from leaked John Podesta emails and 4chan/Reddit threads, alleging a child-trafficking ring operated by Democratic figures out of the Comet Ping Pong pizzeria in Washington, D.C. — was investigated and found to have no factual basis; D.C. police found no evidence, and on December 4, 2016 Edgar Maddison Welch fired a rifle inside the restaurant looking for the (nonexistent) ring and was sentenced to four years in prison. The theory recirculates as a compilation of "red flags" and a list of suspicious deaths. The recurring list, surfaced again in a March 2026 reel, mixes verifiable facts with contested framings: (1) Natacha Jaitt, an Argentine media personality who named figures in an alleged abuse network during a December 2018 television appearance, posted a tweet on April 5, 2018 reading "AVISO: no me voy a suicidar... así que si eso pasa, NO FUI. Guarden tuit" ("WARNING: I'm not going to kill myself... so if that happens, IT WASN'T ME. Save this tweet"); she was found dead on February 23, 2019. The autopsy reported acute pulmonary edema secondary to multi-organ failure with cocaine and alcohol in her system and no external signs of violence; her family disputed the ruling. (2) Janet Ossebaard, the Dutch maker of the QAnon-aligned "Fall of the Cabal" series, was reported missing and found dead in Lund, Sweden on December 22, 2023; reports indicate suicide, her last messages expressing suicidal thoughts. (3) Isaac Kappy, an American actor who in 2018-19 publicly named Hollywood figures as part of an alleged ring, died on May 13, 2019 near Bellemont, Arizona; the Arizona Department of Public Safety ruled it a suicide — the reel's own on-screen text concedes Kappy's accusations were never proven. (4) Andrew Breitbart's February 4, 2011 tweet about John Podesta is genuine, and his March 1, 2012 death was ruled natural (heart failure, no foul play) — documented in full at 2012-breitbart-death-001. (5) DJ Avicii (Tim Bergling), whose 2013 music video "For A Better Day" depicts child trafficking, was found dead in Muscat, Oman on April 20, 2018 at age 28; the death was ruled a suicide from self-inflicted injuries, which his family's statement supported. (6) Actress Anne Heche died after an August 5, 2022 car crash in Los Angeles, ruled accidental by the coroner; the reel pairs her crash footage with her posthumous sex-trafficking film "Girl in Room 13" — documented in full at 2022-anne-heche-death-001. (7) "Frazzledrip" — an alleged video of Hillary Clinton supposedly recovered from Anthony Weiner's laptop — does not exist; it was fabricated by the fake-news site YourNewsWire in 2018, its purported frames traced to an unrelated Indian-restaurant website. The reel also strings together four documented criminal convictions of media figures, recorded separately: ABC News producer James Gordon Meek, former Recount editor Slade Sohmer, former Ars Technica editor Peter Bright (@DrPizza), and former CNN producer John Griffin.

notes: Group-B record, built on the 1999-clinton-body-count-reel-001 model: each named death/event is real and verifiable; the framing that the chain proves a covered-up trafficking ring is contested or, for Frazzledrip, demonstrably fabricated. Pizzagate's underlying ring allegation was investigated and unsubstantiated (the Comet Ping Pong shooting is the documented real-world consequence). Jaitt's tweet and death are both real; the official autopsy ruled non-homicidal (cocaine/alcohol, multi-organ failure), her family contested it — both sides on the record, reader weighs. Ossebaard and Kappy deaths were officially ruled suicides; the reel itself admits Kappy's Hollywood accusations were never proven (a Group-C tell surfaced on its own card). Frazzledrip is a known hoax — notably, the reel even shows the Newsweek debunk headline on screen while implying the video is real. The four genuinely verified criminal facts — the Meek, Sohmer, Bright, and Griffin convictions — are split out as Group-A records (2023-meek-csam-conviction-001, 2025-sohmer-csam-conviction-001, 2020-bright-enticement-001, 2023-griffin-csam-conviction-001) and not asserted as proof of the broader theory. Avicii's death was ruled suicide (Oman, 2018); Anne Heche's was ruled accidental (LA, 2022, detailed at 2022-anne-heche-death-001); Breitbart's was heart failure (2012, detailed at 2012-breitbart-death-001) — each real, each officially non-homicidal. Corpus check: none of these names appear in the released DOJ Epstein-files corpus except Meek, and only as an unrelated ABC byline plus the FBI news-briefing report of his own CSAM plea (see 2023-meek-csam-conviction-001). Anchor y2019 (Clinton/Epstein-network cluster); year=2016 marks Pizzagate's emergence.
